title: GH#39002: perf(git-shim): resolve symlink chains with one readlink spawn (Resolves #39002, Ref #38918)
body:
## Summary

Shim self-resolution and native-git candidate resolution use one readlink -f spawn per symlink chain instead of one per hop, with the hop loop kept as fallback. No verdict, policy or cache changes. Threat model: resolution still follows symlinks to the real file and the shim-sibling guard check is unchanged, so a shim cannot be mistaken for native git; nothing persists across processes. title: GH#39006: fix(recovery): pending --count leaves the supervisor cursor before the first counted entry
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39006

`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` runs `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending --count` just before it writes the `blocker_recovery` trigger. The count shared `pending_cursor` with the supervisor's own `pending` pass and saved the cursor past every entry it checked. The supervisor's pass then started after exactly the entries that justified the run, and those entries waited a full queue wrap. Every logged trigger count on this runner was a partial scan of 1–7 entries (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`), so most of each run's reachable work was the part the count had already passed.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
  - In `--count` mode, each tier's cursor still advances past non-actionable entries. At the first entry the count would emit, the cursor goes back to the value just before it, and the cursor stays there for the rest of that tier. The count is still reported in full.
  - New `_tbr_restore_cursor`: an empty value removes the cursor file, which is the same as starting at the beginning of the queue.
  - The per-tier scan moved into `_tbr_pending_scan_tier`, the same pattern as `_tbr_pending_discovery_stages`, so `tbr_pending` stays under the 100-line function limit. `break 3` became `return 3`; a cursor write failure still makes `tbr_pending` return 2.
  - Plain `pending` and `--rearm-only` (`rearm_cursor`) behave exactly as before.
- `TODO.md`: t19103 recorded; t19100 marked done (GH#38990 closed by PR #38992).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, which sources the capability and discovery suites: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`.
- Ad hoc check that stubs the entry checks over a 5-entry queue (not committed):
  - Count stops the cursor before the first counted entry.
  - Plain `pending` then starts at that entry and still advances.
  - After a wrap, the count restores the pre-wrap cursor.
  - When the first entry is the counted one, the cursor file is removed.
  - A count with nothing actionable advances through the whole queue.
  - All checks pass on this branch. Against `main`, "count stops before first actionable" fails: the cursor ends past the counted entry, which reproduces the defect.

## Risk

Low. The change only affects the `--count` probe's cursor writes. If the supervisor's run never happens (cooldown or failure), the next probe walks the same window again and triggers again, which is the intended retry.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: GH#39008: fix(pulse): re-probe blocker recovery after a partial zero-count scan instead of waiting the full interval
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39008

`_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` stamps its 3h interval, then runs a budget-bounded `pending --count` walk over part of the recovery queue. When that partial walk found nothing, the next probe still waited the full 3h, so one walk of a ~125-entry queue took about a day. On this runner, in the week to 2026-11-18, `trigger=blocker_recovery` starts had gaps of 51h and 27h, against an interval that allows 8 runs a day. Every logged trigger count was a partial scan.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`
  - New `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe`. After a partial (rc 2) zero-count probe, it writes an absolute deadline (`now + PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_PARTIAL_PROBE_INTERVAL`, default 600s, the rearm cadence) to `last_blocker_recovery_partial_due_epoch`, then logs one line: `blocker recovery probe found 0 pending (partial scan); re-probe in 600s`.
  - The full-interval stamp is not rewritten.
  - The interval is parsed as decimal, so `0600` means 600s.
  - No deadline is written when the partial interval is not below the current interval, or when cached API pressure is active.
  - `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` treats the probe as due when the interval has elapsed or the partial deadline has passed. It still checks the failure cooldown first, and it clears the deadline when a probe starts.
  - The deadline holds even if the interval changes before it is reached, for example a 1800s failure-retry interval followed by a success that restores 10800s.
  - A failed or truncated deadline write reads as 0: no early probe, and the full interval is kept.
  - New `_pulse_blocker_api_pressure_active`: the GraphQL circuit-breaker and secondary-cooldown guard, extracted from `_pulse_rearm_blocker_holds`, which now calls it with the same behaviour.
  - A complete zero-count scan, any positive count, and the failure-retry interval behave as before.

Pairs with #39007 (GH#39006). That PR keeps the count from moving the supervisor's cursor past counted entries; without it, faster probes would skip more entries.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: `19/19 tests passed`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`, including "mechanical rearm cadence ... respects API cooldown and circuit state".
- An ad hoc stub-helper check of the real `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` (not committed) passed 16/16:
  - partial zero-count: no trigger, stamp unchanged, deadline at +600s, log line written;
  - not due at +599s; the probe runs at +600s and clears the deadline;
  - complete zero-count: no deadline;
  - partial positive count triggers;
  - circuit-breaker state: no deadline;
  - partial interval at or above the current interval: no deadline;
  - `0600` is read as decimal;
  - a deadline written under the 1800s retry interval still fires at +600s after the interval grows to 10800s;
  - a failed deadline write keeps the full interval and logs nothing.

## Risk

Low. While the queue holds nothing actionable, probes run about every 10 minutes, the same GitHub read cost as the existing 10-minute rearm pass. They stop as soon as a probe finds work, because the trigger then takes the normal interval.

title: t19105: fix(recovery): reserve a queue share for decided holds so replies, policy changes and retries can wake them
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39010

`tbr_pending` scans tier 0 (entries without a standing `human_decision`) through a full rotation before tier 1 (decided entries) starts (GH#38692). Both tiers share one queue deadline. On a live runner, tier 0 never finishes inside the ~29s pending window or the 45s rearm window. `pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` had never been written, although `_tbr_pending_scan_tier` saves the tier cursor before every entry check.

The effect: every positive wake signal for a decided hold lives in tier 1, and none of them could fire. That covers a maintainer reply newer than the decision (GH#38311), a changed repo recovery policy (t19068), and a trusted retry or brief revision in rearm mode. A maintainer who answered a decision packet got no action. Current example: 14 `human_decision` records in one managed repo carry no policy fingerprint, although that repo now declares a recovery policy; none has been re-assessed.

## Changes

All changes are in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`.

- **`_tbr_pending_classify`** classifies the queue once per run. It uses two batched jq reads (queue identities, then decision wakes), so the process count stays constant: 129 entries take ~40 ms, against ~1.5 s for per-entry reads. An unreadable file falls back to the per-entry check, never to a guessed tier.
- **`_tbr_pending_reserve`** applies when any entry is decided. Tier 0 ends `max(1, remaining / 4)` seconds early once at least 2 seconds remain; a single second goes to tier 0. With no decided entries, tier 0 keeps the whole window.
- **`_tbr_pending_scan_tier`** shadows `TBR_QUEUE_DEADLINE` for tier 0, so identity and entry stages cannot run into tier 1's share.
  - At its deadline, tier 0 logs `reason=budget_exhausted tier=0 (decided-tier share reserved)` and returns 4. The run is marked incomplete only if entries remain unobserved.
  - The queue deadline still stops both tiers (rc 3).
  - Entries already observed this run are skipped.
- **Tier-0 resume.** When tier 1 finishes early, tier 0 resumes in the time left, so the reservation never sits idle. A `--count` probe that already counted a tier-0 entry does not resume; its GH#39006 cursor hold stays in place.
- **`_tbr_pending_park`** handles a tier-0 entry that the reservation itself cut short. It parks the cursor just before the entry and writes a `<cursor>_full_window` marker, and the next run gives tier 0 the whole window. A pending pass clears the marker; a `--count` probe only reads it. Without this, an entry needing more than the tier-0 share would time out on every pulse. Worst case, an entry needing more than the whole window alternates between reserved and full-window runs.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `Tests run: 62 failed: 0`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`: `35 run, 0 failed`.
- Ad hoc reproduction (8s budget, 1s per check, 18 undecided + 2 decided entries). On `main`, the decided tier was never reached and no `*_cursor_decided` file was written. On this branch, a decided entry was checked in rearm mode, both decided cursors were written, and the tier-0 share message was logged. With no decided entries, tier 0 still used the full window.
- Review-fix checks, each passing in 3 consecutive runs:
  - batched/per-entry classification parity, including malformed files;
  - tier-0 stage deadline below tier 1's;
  - identity yield;
  - tier-0 resume with no duplicate checks;
  - 3s window (tier 1 reached) and 1s window (no reservation);
  - three-run parking: cut and parked, full window and completed, rotation moved on.
- GH#39006 count-cursor checks: 7/7.

## After deploy

`pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` should appear in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery/` within one pulse cycle. Decided records without a policy fingerprint, in a repo that now has a policy, should then be re-assessed.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: t19106: fix(pulse): early blocker re-probe rechecks API pressure and follows only queue-side partial scans
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #39009 (GH#39008), from its review on #39011. In two cases the early blocker-recovery re-probe fired when it should not have:

1. **Pressure that starts after the deadline was saved.** `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe` checked cached API pressure only when it saved the early deadline. If pressure started later, the early probe still ran at the deadline. `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` now rechecks pressure when it reaches a saved partial deadline. It keeps the deadline, so the probe runs once pressure clears.
2. **Partial scans caused only by discovery.** `pending --count` returns 2 for any incomplete stage. The bounded seed spans every pulse repo and rarely finishes in one call, so a run that finished its queue pass could still schedule a probe every partial interval. The probe's stderr is now saved to `last_blocker_recovery_probe.err`. An early probe is scheduled only when the helper reports a queue-side stage as incomplete (`queue`, `identity` or `entry`). Discovery-only partials (`seed`, `holds`, `unclassified`) keep the full interval. Missing or unreadable stderr also means no early probe, the existing safe default.

Resolves #39012

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe` takes an `err_file` argument and requires a queue-side marker. `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` rechecks pressure at the partial deadline and saves the probe's stderr.
- NEW `todo/tasks/t19106-brief.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: pass.
- Ad hoc partial-probe checks: pass. Queue-side markers schedule the probe. Discovery-only markers, empty stderr and a missing file do not. Pressure at the deadline defers the probe and keeps the deadline, and it fires once pressure clears.
- Compatible with #39011: its tier-0 yield line (`incomplete stage=queue ... tier=0`) matches the queue-side pattern.

On a managed product repo, two issues that a completion-phase worker reopened because of sibling gaps were not attempted for 10-16h, while the dispatcher made several hundred attempts on other issues.

- `_action_rsd_single`: an `available` heal of open + `status:done` now removes assignees whose last assignment predates the latest reopen. A new helper, `_pir_prior_lifecycle_assignees`, reads issue events once. If the issue was never reopened, the events read fails, or a timestamp is malformed, every assignee is kept. A failed combined edit falls back to the status-only heal, so cleanup can never block the heal. A `blocked` restore keeps its assignees.
- `_dispatch_order_claim_state_candidates` (GH#38333 fresh-first lane): an assignee no longer counts as a claim when dedup would treat it as passive. That means only self, repo owner or repo maintainer, no queued/in-progress/in-review/claimed label, and no `origin:interactive` without `auto-dispatch`. This mirrors `_has_active_claim` and `_is_assigned_compute_blocking`. Such candidates pass the assignee gate cheaply, so the 27-75s rejection cost that motivated GH#38333 does not apply to them. If the maintainer map cannot be read, the stricter rule is kept. The log line now also counts kept candidates.

Resolves #39030

## Verification

- `shellcheck` is clean on both files.
- `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` passes, including the GH#38333 ordering case.
- `test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh` passes, as do `test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` (37/37) and `test-reconcile-budget-isolation.sh` (8/8).
- An ad hoc harness (16/16, run twice) runs the real `_action_rsd_single` with stubbed `gh` events. It covers:
  - a prior assignee removed while a post-reopen assignee is kept
  - both prior assignees removed
  - a never-reopened issue
  - a failed events read
  - a malformed timestamp
  - an unrelated event row ignored
  - a combined-edit failure falling back
  - a blocked restore
  - an unassigned issue

  The same harness runs the real `_dispatch_order_claim_state_candidates` on 12 fixtures (self, owner, maintainer, teammate, queued, interactive hold, auto-dispatch handoff, mixed, foreign-repo maintainer, object-shaped assignee, label-only claim). The missing-map and invalid-JSON cases pass too.
- A read-only run of the real helper against live issues returns the stale maintainer assignee for both starved reopened issues and nothing for two never-reopened assigned issues.

After deploy, check `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` for "removed prior-lifecycle assignees" on heals and for "passive-assignee candidate(s) kept fresh" in the fresh-first lane line.

title: t19111: fix(worktree-deps): skip Spotlight marker and tool-cache entries at node_modules root instead of rejecting the restore
body:
## Summary

Dependency provisioning for worker worktrees rejected sources whose `node_modules` root held non-module entries created by macOS or build tools: a Spotlight `.metadata_never_index` marker, `.DS_Store`, and Vite or other tool caches (`.vite`, `.vite-temp`, `.cache`). `resolution_root()` treated each of them as a package root, so `check_package_root()` raised `unrecorded-module-file`. On one managed pnpm repo that accounted for 330 of the last 406 rejections in the pulse log.

- `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`: a typed allowlist of top-level entries that are skipped: neither counted, copied, recorded nor inventoried, exactly like the existing interrupted pnpm staging skip. Marker names are skipped only as regular files, and cache names only as real directories (lstat, so never symlinks).
- The trust boundary is unchanged. Node resolves bare specifiers such as `require('.extra.js')` to `node_modules/.extra.js`, so any other unrecorded entry, and any allowlisted name with another type, still rejects. A worker cannot resolve a skipped entry, because it is never copied.

Scope, measured: that repo's source `node_modules` is about 3.9 GB, against the 64 MiB copy budget. With this fix it will reject on the byte or entry budget, or on `stale-installed-lock` (the current read-only result) instead. Workers there keep installing from the lockfile per `workflows/full-loop.md`. This PR removes the false rejection for sources that fit the budget. Fast provisioning for large pnpm sources is separate work.

Resolves #39037

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`: 32/32 pass. The new `test_root_markers_and_tool_caches_are_skipped` runs the real restore path for npm and pnpm with all five entries present. It asserts that the package was copied and none of the entries were. It then asserts that a symlinked `.cache` and a directory named `.metadata_never_index` still refuse the restore. The existing `.extra.js` rejection case is unchanged.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on both files.
- Read-only run against the real pnpm source, deployed versus patched validator: both currently stop earlier at `stale-installed-lock`. The canonical install is behind its lockfile, so the restore is refused before the walk either way.

title: GH#39034: share census attestation with the removal-guard observer and surface cleanup refusal reasons
body:
## Summary

A (shared attestation): worktree_process_proc.py now excludes a denied same-UID process only when every thread passes worktree_process_attestation.session_class(), the predicate the lease census already uses (GH#38428). Preconditions match the census: Linux, the attestation /proc root, require_proc_visibility() (PID namespace, no hidepid), plus the per-task non-root and initial-user-namespace checks inside session_class. Applies to collect() (paths/denied, maintenance boundary) and cwd_map_line() (shared procfs loop). No name-based exclusions; any miss, error or failed precondition leaves the process denied. B (refusal visibility): cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh counts every refused worktree in the pass once (last final skip reason, else its degraded reason; a later removal clears it), prints refused=N and skip_reasons=<top 5 reason:count>, and logs outcome=no-progress when candidates were refused and nothing was removed or archived. The finished-worktree reclaim line adds reasons=<top 5> from .results[] decision=refuse. storage-cleanup-helper.sh shows the last pass's refused count and reasons next to 'Linked worktrees: N'. C (unambiguous degraded log): the degraded guard result now logs worktree-degraded: ... cwd-visibility-degraded ... mode=recoverable-required; only a final refusal logs worktree-skipped. Docs: reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md, .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh, .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-process-census.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py

## Decisions

Per the scoped review: no interactive-worktree enrolment, operator attestation command or name exemptions. Every thread must attest (stricter than the census, which skips fully foreign threads), keeping the observer fail-closed. The async summary counts per worktree, and a degraded event without a final skip counts as a refusal because several callers return the degraded guard result without logging one. Not exercised against a real systemd --user manager (needs a systemd host); the user-manager and pam-keeper paths are covered by the shared modelled-kernel tests. title: GH#39048: fix(permission-broker): allow designed bounded-operation polls through OpenCode doom_loop
body:
## Summary

Headless workers that fan out identical read-only aidevops_bounded_operation status/output polls in one response hit OpenCode doom_loop; the broker rejected it as non-grantable and the worker session ended with permission_required, losing finished work (six such failures on 2026-11-18). The broker now answers only that designed-poll doom loop with once/allow and records a non-blocking permission_designed_poll_allowed event; start/cancel repeats, other tools, and interactive sessions keep the existing gate.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-designed-poll.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19113-brief.md

The prompt starts `aidevops_bounded_operation` (`sleep 40`) and then emits three byte-identical `status` polls in one response — the same pattern the OpenCode session DB shows for the failed workers.

- **Unpatched (deployed plugin):** CLI prints `permission requested: doom_loop (aidevops_bounded_operation); auto-rejecting`, then `error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.` The session ends before its final reply. This reproduces the production failure.
- **Patched (this branch):** the same doom_loop ask is raised; all three status polls complete, and the session finishes with `PROBE_RESULT=3`. The blocker log records one `permission_designed_poll_allowed` event (`risk_level: low`, `blocking: false`) and no non-grantable capture.

Trigger, read from the installed binary: `doom_loop` fires only when the last 3 parts of the current assistant message are identical tool calls with the same input. Sequential polls across steps never reach it.

title: GH#38959: key OAuth pool seats by email + Anthropic org (Team + Personal on one email)
body:
## Summary

OAuth pool identity is now a seat: email plus optional Anthropic orgId (key `email#orgId`; legacy entries without orgId keep the email-only key). A Team and a Personal grant on the same email become separate seats that rotate independently. New grants take their org from the token response, falling back to the profile endpoint. When an email has one legacy no-org seat, its org is resolved with that seat's own unexpired token (never refreshed); a different org adds a seat ('split'), an unresolved one updates in place with a warning. A grant without org for a multi-seat email is refused and parked as pending. A grant without org that updates a single org-tagged seat keeps that seat's org. Same-email CRUD (remove, set-priority, assign-pending, remote-sync get/put) takes `--org` (orgId prefix or org name, case-insensitive) and refuses ambiguity instead of acting on the first match. JS covers storage, provider-auth (V1/V2), proxy retry/cooldowns, rotation probe and display; Python covers CRUD, rotate, refresh, health and entry-sync; shell covers add/manage/remote-sync/diagnose. The headless worker pre-dispatch check now matches the pool row by access token first and uses email only when it names exactly one seat. Seat targeting lives in the new `oauth-pool-anthropic-org.mjs` and `oauth-pool-lib/_seat_upsert.py`. OpenAI `accountId` stays metadata, not a match key. Docs: opencode-anthropic-auth.md, oauth-pool-remote-sync.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-jsonpath.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-retry.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-streaming.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-account-actions.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-anthropic-org.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-auth-handlers.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-callback.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-constants.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-display.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-health-check.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-refresh.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-storage.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-pool-recovery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-pool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-provider-auth.mjs, .agents/reference/oauth-pool-remote-sync.md, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-invocation.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-diagnose.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/_common.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/_seat_upsert.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_accounts.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_entry_sync.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_health.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_refresh.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_rotate.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_token_utils.py, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-manage.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-remote-sync.sh, .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs, .agents/tools/opencode/opencode-anthropic-auth.md

title: GH#39023: fix: preserve init project config written from a linked worktree
body:
## Summary

aidevops init in a linked worktree writes the ignored .aidevops.json only to that worktree, so it was lost when the worktree was removed. Only the terminal confirmation is skipped, and only for that framework-owned, user-owned, mode-600 file; the boundary is recorded in the helper. An existing canonical config is never overwritten; the copy is removed after a restore, when a canonical config exists, or when the slug is no longer registered. The onboarding advisory now recommends restore instead of re-running init when the registry shows a previous init, and reference/repo-onboarding.md documents the order for repos that are already affected (merge the .gitignore rule, then restore).

title: t19114: fix(checkpoints): resume a continuation review worktree that is only ahead of the PR head
body:
## Summary

A checkpoint continuation worker commits locally and pushes once at the end. When it exited before that push, its clean review worktree was the verified PR head plus unpushed commits. _prrts_reconcile_existing_worktree_head only accepted a worktree behind the PR head, so every later continuation dispatch refused it as existing_review_worktree_diverged and the draft stayed stranded. New helper _prrts_resume_ahead_continuation_worktree in pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh runs after the existing claim, dirty-state preservation, exact-head fetch and clean/branch re-check. When the dispatch has a linked issue (checkpoint continuation) and HEAD contains the verified head with at least one extra commit, it keeps the worktree, logs the resumed commit count and returns 0. The continuation prompt already tells the worker to keep and verify unpushed commits, and its single non-force push still fast-forwards the unchanged remote head behind the exact-target fence.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19114-brief.md

## Decisions

Scoped to checkpoint continuations only, because ordinary review-thread workers have no resume contract in their prompt. No new test fixture: the stub-git suite cannot express ancestry direction without new stub modes, and the real-git harness covered the behaviour more cheaply.

title: t19115: fix(checkpoints): a trusted terminal-blocker re-arm releases a blocked worker draft
body:
## Summary

Terminal-blocker recovery re-arms a held issue for a maintainer retry (trusted_retry) or a revision after the blocker (revision_changed) and projects status:available. When the blocked worker left a draft, the draft still held the issue until someone copied a revision-bound approval line, so even a maintainer retry directive was ignored. A census of open blocked-checkpoint drafts found 4 of 9 already re-armed with refusal=none and no approval; one had waited more than 50 hours. `_pcc_policy_route` now calls the new `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` before the unknown-triage route. It publishes the existing approval line once per receipt when: the newest unedited receipt after the blocked release is trusted_retry or revision_changed; the receipt poster, publisher and runner have write permission; trusted_retry also has an unedited OWNER/MEMBER retry directive from a write-authorised login between the release and the receipt; revision_changed has a write-authorised issue author (only the author or a write collaborator can edit the body); the issue is open, unassigned, auto-dispatchable and unheld; the draft is eligible; and the template binds the current head and brief SHA. A native ref `refs/aidevops/checkpoint-rearm/ISSUE/RECEIPT` makes publication at-most-once across runners. Permission-window and lifecycle re-arms never qualify. Repos opt out with `checkpoint_policy.auto_continue_rearmed: false`. `dispatch-approved` keeps every continuation gate. Design refinement over the filed brief: revision_changed publishes on author trust instead of requiring the unknown-work policy. The motivating draft is a revision_changed case, and the re-arm already treats that revision as release-worthy for ordinary dispatch. The brief update is in planning PR #39079. Also extracts `_pcc_logins_have_write` and `_pcc_create_audit_ref` to share permission and ref-creation code, and fixes a pre-existing MD012 in the reference doc.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh: All 217 tests passed. This includes the new t19115 case: trusted retry and trusted revision publish exactly one approval, a lost reservation never republishes, and a valid approval short-circuits. Rejected without publishing: non-write poster, retry author or issue author; COLLABORATOR or edited retry; older or edited receipt; permission-window and lifecycle reasons; moved head; assigned or held issue; opted-out repo. _pcc_policy_route prefers the re-arm over unknown triage and falls through for non-qualifying reasons. The existing decision-policy and unknown-policy suites pass after the shared-helper refactor. ShellCheck is clean on all three shell files; markdownlint is clean on the reference doc. After the rebase, no new main commit touches the checkpoint files.

Resolves #39077

title: t19116: perf(pulse): take the dispatch launch slot at the claim so rejections evaluate in parallel
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39087

`_dispatch_max_loop` reserved a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony, and the ceremony cap was clamped to the free-slot count. Most candidates are rejected by read-only dedup layers long before the first persistent write. On a busy runner with few free slots, rejections were therefore evaluated one at a time while 80–110 candidates waited. The evidence is in the issue: average occupancy was about 6–7 workers against a target of 20, 22% of capacity samples had zero workers, and one cycle ran 37 candidates strictly in sequence.

This PR moves the reservation to the claim point:

- **Launch-slot semaphore** (`pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`). `_dispatch_max_loop` owns a private slot directory (budget = `effective_slots`). `_dispatch_launch_slot_acquire` takes `slot.N` atomically with `mkdir`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_settle` keeps the slot on rc 0 (launched) or rc 124 (state unknown after the timeout kill) and releases it on any other rc. A success that bypassed the claim point takes an overflow slot, and acquire backs off when overflow would exceed the budget. Without a loop-owned directory (serial loop, direct callers), acquire always succeeds and behaviour does not change.
- **Claim-point acquire** (`pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`). `_dlw_claim_slot_and_lock` takes the slot immediately before `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`, which is the first persistent claim write. If every slot is held, it returns rc 75 (`_DISPATCH_CYCLE_BUDGET_DEFER_RC`). That rc's existing path records a deferral and clears the attempt-recency stamp. It writes no claim and records no fast-fail, backoff or negative cache. The outcome line reads `reason=launch_slot_full`.
- **Evaluation concurrency** (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`). `_dispatch_eval_parallel_cap` returns `slots × DISPATCH_EVAL_OVERSUBSCRIBE` (default 3) and replaces the bare slot clamp in `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase`, so 1- and 2-slot rounds no longer drop to serial. `DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL` (default 6), the throttle file, a forced floor and REST-core serial mode keep their caps. `_dispatch_max_await_slot` waits for a free launch slot instead of a ceremony reservation. It ends the round when every slot is held and nothing is in flight.
- **Opt-out**: `DISPATCH_LAUNCH_SLOT_GATE=0` restores the ceremony-start reservation and the slot clamp exactly. This is documented in `.agents/reference/configuration.md`.

Scope note: the brief named `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` for the helpers. They live in `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, beside the other capacity helpers, and the claim wrapper lives in `pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`, beside `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`: 90/90 pass. New cases:
  - A 1-slot round evaluates candidates concurrently (peak ≥ 2), launches exactly one and defers the rest with `rc=75|reason=launch_slot_full`, with zero failures.
  - A holder whose claim fails releases its slot, and a later candidate launches.
  - `_dlw_claim_slot_and_lock` contract: it defers without a claim, claims when a slot is free, returns 2 on a claim failure (slot released), and treats overflow as consumed budget.
  - The 4-slot budget holds with the gate on and off. The parallel cap oversubscribes ×3, and the legacy and forced-floor modes keep the slot cap.
  - Priority-loop stubs now pass the claim point like production launches.
- These suites pass unchanged: `test-dispatch-min-concurrency`, `test-runner-capability`, `test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing`, `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve`, `test-pulse-dispatch-core-pr-target-guard`, `test-status-label-state-machine`, `test-precreation-failure-skip`, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave`, `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot`, `test-pulse-dispatch-stage-rc-adapter`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection`.
- ShellCheck is clean on all changed scripts. markdownlint is clean. The pre-commit ratchets pass.

## Post-deploy check

`rg 'loop body finished' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail` should show `mode=parallel(N)` with N above the free-slot count in low-slot rounds, and `launch_slot_full` deferrals should stay a small fraction of the candidates processed. Over 12 hours, the occupancy census (`worker-occupancy.sh`) should show the average concurrent workers rising from the ~6–7 baseline.

title: GH#39095: fix(model-availability): treat a usable OAuth pool account as provider auth on OpenCode 2
body:
Resolves #39095

## Problem

On OpenCode 2.x the model availability probe reports every provider as `no-key`, so `resolve standard` / `resolve thinking` fail and Pulse never dispatches a worker. `resolve_api_key` only reads `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` for OAuth, and OpenCode 2 keeps credentials in its own database and does not write that file. The aidevops OAuth pool (`~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json`) was only used to *block* a provider (cooldown / all-auth-error), never as a positive credential signal.

## Change

`.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`

- Adds Source 5 to `resolve_api_key`: when the OAuth pool holds at least one account for the provider that is neither `auth-error` nor inside an active `rate-limited` cooldown, return the existing `oauth-refresh-available` marker with `RESOLVED_API_KEY_SOURCE=oauth-pool:<provider>`. This reuses the Source 4 OAuth path (record healthy, skip the HTTP probe), so no probe-lib changes are needed.
- New read-only helper `_resolve_oauth_pool_available` (honours `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE`, same selection rules as `_probe_oauth_pool_cooldown_gate`, never prints credential material).
- Sources 1-4 keep priority, so env/gopass/credentials/auth.json behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

On macOS, OpenCode v2.3.0, one healthy Anthropic pool account, no `auth.json`:

- Before: `probe anthropic --force` → `no API key configured`; `resolve standard` → `No available model for tier: standard`.
- After: `probe anthropic --force` → `OAuth refresh token available`, `1 healthy`; `resolve standard` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`; `resolve thinking` → `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.
- Negative: `probe openai --force` (no pool accounts) → still `1 no key`; `MODEL_AVAILABILITY_OAUTH_POOL_FILE=/nonexistent probe anthropic --force` → still `1 no key`.
- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` clean; pre-commit validation passed.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh` → 32 run, 0 failed.

No new tests added (existing suite covers the auth.json/static-auth paths; happy to add a pool-file case if wanted).

title: GH#39027: fix: print sudo-resolvable approval commands on Linux user-local installs
body:
## Summary

Linux sudoers secure_path omits ~/.local/bin, so every printed `sudo aidevops approve ...` command failed with `sudo: aidevops: command not found` on user-local installs. New `approval_cli_prefix` (`.agents/scripts/shared-approval-cli.sh`, sourced by `shared-constants.sh`; Python mirror in `command_policy_approval.py`; added to the worker-lifecycle bundle) prints `sudo aidevops` on macOS or whenever sudo can already resolve the CLI, otherwise the launcher path (tilde-relative under the user's home, e.g. `sudo ~/.local/bin/aidevops`). Unsafe or unresolvable paths fall back to `sudo aidevops`. All approval-command printing sites (approval helper help/commands/permissions, worker-permission-helper, pulse NMR/merge-gates/diagnose/reconcile/dependabot/triage, full-loop merge/readiness, dispatch policy, quality-feedback, Cloudron release approval, pulse-check report) now use the renderer. Content matchers (ever-NMR canonical text, triage noise filter, Cloudron finalized-body check) accept only the renderer-approved prefix forms. Signed Cloudron policy text keeps its placeholder line byte-stable. The ever-NMR jq def moved into its own printer (`_approval_snapshot_v2_ever_nmr_filters`, same pattern as the terminal-blocker filters) to keep `_approval_snapshot_v2_comments_json` under the 100-line function limit. `reference/auto-merge.md` and `reference/dispatch-blockers.md` note the Linux launcher form.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/auto-merge.md, .agents/reference/dispatch-blockers.md, .agents/scripts/approval-helper-commands.sh, .agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh, .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh, .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/command_policy_approval.py, .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-policy.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-check-report.jq, .agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-issue.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh, .agents/scripts/quality-feedback-issues-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-approval-cli.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-prompts-repo-qualified.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-approval.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py

## Decisions

Render rather than change install layout: sudo secure_path is system policy, so printing the resolvable launcher path is the least invasive fix. The renderer accepts only `sudo aidevops`, `sudo ~/...aidevops` or `sudo /...aidevops`, so matchers stay strict and paste-safe. Byte-exact signed Cloudron bodies are not rewritten. The sudo-user home lookup uses getent, then the exact /etc/passwd entry, and never guesses a path.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Ubuntu 24.04 Docker end-to-end, with secure_path=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/snap/bin and the CLI at ~/.local/bin: the legacy `sudo aidevops approve ...` fails with `command not found`. The real `approval-helper.sh help` output now prints `sudo ~/.local/bin/aidevops approve setup`, and pasting that line runs the launcher as uid 0. Under sudo with getent unavailable, the home directory resolves from /etc/passwd and the prefix stays tilde-relative. The Python mirror renders the same prefix. macOS renders unchanged `sudo aidevops`. 16 focused existing tests pass (approval helper, permissions module, pulse NMR/diagnose/dependabot/reconcile/merge gates, full-loop merge authority, dispatch policy, quality-feedback, shared-constants, worker launch bundle). After rebasing on origin/main and extracting the ever-NMR filter, test-approval-helper-content-binding, test-pulse-nmr-approval, test-approval-helper-verify-state, test-approval-prompts-repo-qualified and test-pulse-nmr-maintainer-authority pass. ShellCheck clean; function-complexity gate reports no new violations; `python3 -m unittest tests.test_bundle` passes; diff-scoped pipe-early-exit-check clean. Pre-existing, unrelated failures reproduce identically on base c7757722 and are filed: #39105 (test-failure-family-remediation `$delivery`) and #39106 (test-worker-briefed-trust-parity silent exit).

Resolves #39027

title: GH#39028: fix(approval): kick the managed pulse with the user session bus after sudo approvals
body:
## Summary

sudo -u resets the environment, so the full pulse kicked after a sudo permission approval/withdrawal had no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, held the pulse lock, and every systemd worker launch failed with manager_probe_failed. The permission kick now asks a loaded systemd user supervisor to start aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service (Linux only, run as the real user with its /run/user/<uid> session bus) and only falls back to a detached spawn, which now carries the same session env. The issue-approval --merge-only kick shares the env-carrying spawn. macOS/launchd behaviour is unchanged. Refusing the dispatch lock when the backend probe fails is tracked separately in #39118.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh, .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on Linux (Debian container via OrbStack): real sudo env reset, real user alice uid 1000 with /run/user/1000 and a live bus socket, real approval-helper.sh sourced under sudo from that user, pulse-wrapper.sh replaced by an env recorder. origin/main reproduces the bug: kicked pulse-wrapper ran with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<unset> DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=<unset> (also for the --merge-only kick). Fixed tree: spawn fallback and --merge-only kick run as alice with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus; with a systemctl recorder on PATH the permission kick instead runs systemctl --user start --no-block aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service as alice with the same env. macOS: sourced probe confirms Darwin skips the managed path. test-approve-kicks-pulse.sh 36/36, test-approval-helper-rest-lock-fallback.sh 83/83, shellcheck clean. A real systemd user manager was not run in the container.

## Regression Evidence

An automated regression test is not practical in the repository suites: the defect only appears when `sudo` resets the environment for a non-root user who owns a real `/run/user/<uid>` runtime directory and session bus socket. That needs root, a second real account, and a Linux user runtime directory, none of which exist on the macOS developer hosts or the unprivileged GitHub runner test harness, and the existing stubbed suites (`test-approve-kicks-pulse.sh`, `test-approval-helper-rest-lock-fallback.sh`) bypass `sudo` entirely.

The same before/after comparison was run instead as a disposable container probe (Debian, `python:3-slim`, real `sudo`, user `alice` uid 1000 with a bound `/run/user/1000/bus` socket, both trees mounted read-only):

| Case | origin/main | this PR |
|------|-------------|---------|
| Permission kick, no systemd (spawn fallback) | `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<unset> DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=<unset>` | `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus` |
| Issue-approval `--merge-only` kick | `<unset>` / `<unset>` | same session env as above |
| Permission kick, systemd user unit present | spawned `pulse-wrapper.sh` without env | `systemctl --user start --no-block aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service` as `alice` with the session env |

Resolves #39028

title: t19122: perf(pulse): let a running dispatch round absorb worker slots freed mid-round
body:
## Summary

A parallel max-path round sizes its slot budget once, then runs for tens of minutes; worker exits during the round record the event-refill trigger, but the refill cannot take the instance lock the round holds (lock_busy), so freed slots idled until the next round. When the worker-exit trigger is newer than the round's last capacity read, a spent budget now re-reads _dispatch_compute_capacity and rises to launched + free - hold (pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh _dispatch_round_topup_due/_dispatch_round_topup_budget; launch-slot budget file replaced atomically). _dispatch_max_loop/_dispatch_max_await_slot adopt the raised budget; _dispatch_priority_loop tops up at each drained phase boundary; serial reserved pools hold the other pool's share; concurrent pools, floor, throttle and serial rounds never top up. dispatch_max stamps its capacity read through _dispatch_round_capacity_read (function size unchanged at the 100-line gate). Documented in reference/configuration.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/configuration.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Re-read capacity only when the worker-exit trigger mtime is at or after the last read, so idle rounds make no extra process scans. Target counts recorded launches; in-flight launch-slot holders are still subtracted by the existing slot checks, so the cap stays conservative. Concurrent priority pools are excluded because both would claim the same freed slots; the next phase boundary absorbs them. Opt-out DISPATCH_ROUND_TOPUP=0; DISPATCH_ROUND_TOPUP_MAX_ROUND_S (default 1800) ends absorption in long rounds so a fresh census runs. Production occupancy impact is unmeasured until deployed.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh: 98/98 pass, including 7 new round_topup cases (gate on/off top-up 2->5 with 3 mid-round exits; no trigger performs zero capacity re-reads; DISPATCH_ROUND_TOPUP=0 and disallowed loops keep the budget; priority loop launches only past 2 held product slots). test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave, test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot, test-dispatch-min-concurrency, test-pulse-event-refill, test-pulse-ram-admission pass. shellcheck -S style clean on all changed scripts.

Resolves #39128

title: t19133: fix(pulse-watchdog): starved deferrable stages borrow the capped dispatch-reserve fuse so dirty_pr_sweep stops starving
body:
## Summary

A deferrable pulse stage starved longer than `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_DEFERRABLE_BORROW_STARVATION_S` (default 7200s, twice the critical bound; 0 disables) now borrows the same capped dispatch-reserve slice (GH#38840) that starved critical stages use. A deferrable stage that has never started measures the bound from its first deferral: a `<stage>.first_deferral` marker that `_pulse_stage_note_start` clears. A fresh or wiped state dir therefore cannot let every deferrable stage take the shared slice at once.

Evidence: in the retained `pulse.log` since 2026-11-13 (6 days), `dirty_pr_sweep` has 0 `Stage start` lines, 91 cycle-budget deferrals and 53 budget-priority deferrals, and `dirty-pr-sweep-last-run` was last written 2026-09-29. In the same cycles the critical `redirect_spam_sweep`, which runs right after it, was fused with `reserve_borrow=120s`. `dirty_pr_sweep` is the only automated TODO.md-only union rebase for conflicted PRs, so conflicted planning PRs waited for a human session.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19133-brief.md

## Decisions

- The per-cycle borrow stays capped by `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_RESERVE_BORROW_S` (120s) and shared with critical stages, so maximum dispatch loss per cycle is unchanged. The longer deferrable bound lets starved critical stages take the slice first.
- Progress stages and a missing classifier still never borrow. Quota (budget-priority) deferral is unchanged and runs before the cycle clock.
- The independent review found that a never-started deferrable stage (`last == 0`) bypassed the bound. Refusing never-started stages outright would keep `dirty_pr_sweep`, which has no start stamp, starved forever. The bound is therefore anchored at the first deferral instead.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified. I sourced the branch's real `pulse-budget-priority.sh` and `pulse-watchdog.sh` with a real clock, an isolated state dir, a lock owned by the test process, an exhausted cycle clock and a protected 600s dispatch reserve, then ran `run_stage_with_timeout`. Results:
  - The classifier returns `deferrable` for `dirty_pr_sweep`; the borrow helper prints `120 7200` and refuses the progress-class `deterministic_merge_pass`.
  - Never-started `dirty_pr_sweep`: rc 124 and a first-deferral marker is written.
  - Marker 7300s old: `Stage starvation fuse: dirty_pr_sweep last_start_age=7300s timeout=120s fuse_spent=0s reserve_borrow=120s`, Stage start/complete, marker cleared.
  - Immediately after: `Stage deferred: dirty_pr_sweep cycle budget exhausted`.
  - Start stamp 7300s old: fused with `timeout=118s fuse_spent=2s` (shared budget charged).
  - A never-started critical `reap_orphan_workers` still borrows at once.
- **Tests:**
  - `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring` passes (99/0) under the default bash and under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57. The extended borrow contract fails with the watchdog change reverted.
  - These also pass: `test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping`, `test-pulse-diagnose-cycle-health` (42/0), `test-pulse-todo-sync-parallel`, `test-watchdog-no-false-kill` (91/0), `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave`, `test-pulse-watchdog-tick`, `test-pulse-prefetch-stage-budget`, `test-pulse-batch-refresh-timeout`, `test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume` (56/0), `test-pulse-cycle-state-contract` (33/0), `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority`.
  - ShellCheck is clean.

title: GH#39187: perf(gh-shim): remove per-call bash forks from instrumentation, path resolution and cooldown preflight
body:
## Summary

Every gh call on the runner goes through the aidevops shim (~3.4 calls/s; host load 36-74 on 16 CPUs for five days). An xtrace of one REST read showed 102 forked bash subshells, plus external date/jq/perl/sysctl/sed/dirname/basename/cat execs. This removes the avoidable ones without changing records or verdicts. gh-api-instrument.sh: printf -v *_into variants of the field sanitisers, caller resolution, pool/auth defaults and attempt-state temp dir (stdout helpers kept as thin wrappers); _gh_now_ms uses Bash 5 EPOCHREALTIME instead of two perl execs. gh-native-transport-lib.sh: POSIX dirname/basename by parameter expansion in _shim_canonical_path; framework caller labels assigned without capture forks. gh: startup path resolution without dirname/basename and, for clean absolute parents, without the cd subshell. gh-transport-controls.sh: REST timing via _gh_now_ms_into; no cat exec for an empty error file. shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh: builtin clock, jq-free fast path for the cooldown expiry (exact writer shape; anything else still uses jq), builtin boot-time parse in a new pure helper _gh_secondary_kern_boottime_sec, boot probe skipped when the boot window is 0 (the default), no cd/dirname at source time. Result: 102 -> 28-32 forked bash PIDs per REST read; interleaved benchmark (12 reads each, host load ~60) mean CPU 0.448s -> 0.300s per call (-33%), mean wall 3.67s -> 1.57s (wall is noisy at this load).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh, .agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh, .agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19134-brief.md, todo/tasks/t19135-brief.md, todo/tasks/t19136-brief.md

## Decisions

Functions that tests stub (_gh_now_seconds, _gh_secondary_cooldown_now, _gh_secondary_system_boot_ts, _gh_secondary_cooldown_expires_at, _gh_secondary_read_ramp_phase) keep their $(...) call sites so the stubs still govern behaviour; only their bodies got cheaper. gh_new_logical_id and gh_new_attempt_id keep their subshell, because their uniqueness relies on the subshell BASHPID. The GitHub App auth probe stays in a subshell (it only runs when that helper is loaded, which the shim does not do). Latent defect fixed along the way: the old macOS boot-time sed was greedy and returned kern.boottime usec instead of sec, so the gh read boot ramp could never engage; it is disabled by default (AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_RAMP_BOOT_SECS=0), so default behaviour is unchanged. The parse lives in a pure helper so the regression is testable on Linux CI. The same pipeline in pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh is left for GH#39190 to keep this PR scoped. Scope grew from 3 to 5 source files (gh and gh-transport-controls.sh were measured hot-path forks); the brief records this.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: ran the worktree shim on the production runner for real REST reads against api.github.com (gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/29234 --jq .state) under xtrace (forked bash PIDs 102 -> 28-32) and in an interleaved 12-read before/after benchmark against an extracted HEAD copy (CPU 0.448s -> 0.300s per call). New regression cases in test-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh (28/28 pass): kern.boottime text parses to sec not usec (old greedy sed returns 274703 for the same input) plus a plausibility check of the real host boot probe; cooldown expiry fast path matches compact, pretty, escaped-reason and reordered documents; zero or unset boot window skips the boot probe. Existing suites pass: test-gh-api-instrument.sh, test-gh-shim.sh (335/335), test-gh-shim-native-resolution.sh, test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh, test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat.sh, test-gh-pr-checks-exact-json.sh, test-gh-signature-attempt-metrics.sh, test-full-loop-worktree-gh-shim.sh, test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh, test-portable-stat.sh, test-gh-transport-budget.py. test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh scenario 2 fails identically on unmodified main (fixture drift, filed as GH#39189). Ad-hoc parity script on Bash 5.3, /bin/bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9: dirname/basename shapes vs the system tools, sanitiser/pool/auth/caller outputs, ms clock, boot time equals kern.boottime sec, expiry fast path equals jq. ShellCheck clean; pre-commit ratchets including /bin/bash 3.2 parse pass.

Resolves #39187

title: GH#39197: fix(worker-watchdog): defer no-output kills while the worker's isolated DB shows live tool output
body:
## Summary

Workers whose tool streams output for minutes (repository lock waits, long test runs, builds that print) were killed as `watchdog_stall_*`. OpenCode `run --format json` emits a tool event only when the tool part completes, so the output file the watchdog watches stays the same size. Tree CPU stays under 2% and there is no HTTPS socket, so none of the existing deferrals fire. In 24 h on one runner, 18 of 84 stall kills (about 8 worker-hours) were workers waiting on a lock with a heartbeat printing every 2 s. Each kill also lost the worker's place in the lock queue.

OpenCode rewrites the running tool part in the worker's isolated DB as output streams. This PR uses that as one more liveness signal.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh`: new `--worker-db PATH` (env fallback `WORKER_ACTIVITY_DB`) and `_watchdog_db_part_activity`. On a confirmed output stall, a `part.time_updated` within `WORKER_DB_ACTIVITY_WINDOW_SECONDS` (default 120) defers the kill as `reason=tool_output_active signal=worker_db_part_update age=Ns`. The check runs after the CI-wait check and before the more expensive `lsof` network probe. Hard-kill cap timing is unchanged; at the cap this signal classifies as `hard_kill_cap_active`, like the other liveness signals. Fails open: no DB, no `sqlite3`, or a locked or malformed DB returns no deferral. Parts left `running` by a killed earlier attempt never update, so they do not count.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`: passes `--worker-db "${_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH:-}"` to the watchdog.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`: Test 28 gets a stub and an assertion for `tool_output_active` cap classification. New Test 29: (a) a quiet worker with a DB part updated every second is deferred and survives; (b) a DB whose newest part is old does not defer, and the worker is killed.
- Planning: TODO lines for t19137 (already merged in #39196) and t19138, `todo/tasks/t19138-brief.md`, and an MD038 fix in `todo/tasks/t19136-brief.md`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`: 94 tests, 0 failures.
- ShellCheck at warning level is clean on all three shell files. The 6 SC2016 info notices in the test file are also present on `main`. Pre-commit ratchets and the Bash 3.2 parse check passed.
- The probe query was run against 5 live worker isolated DBs with `/usr/bin/sqlite3 -readonly`: all returned rc=0, with the newest part 0–1 s old, including the 3 workers that had a `running` tool part.
- `markdownlint-cli2` on both briefs: 0 issues.

## Runtime check after merge

Count `reason=tool_output_active` in the worker lifecycle logs and compare `watchdog_stall_*` counts in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` over 24 h against the baseline of 84.

Resolves #39197
Ref #39194

## Summary

r915 (`pulse-check-helper.sh apply`, daily 06:20) turns recurring worker failure families into self-improvement issues without a human, but it ran with the interactive `report` budget (45 s total, 10 s per component, 20 s queue). On a loaded host the 24 h worker-history collector timed out at 10 s in 6 of the last 13 runs, and the latest queue scan covered 3/70 repos, so failure-family evidence was empty and every run ended `no autofile findings above thresholds`. `apply` now resolves 300 s / 60 s / 210 s after argument parsing; `report`/`json` keep 45/10/20; `--budget` and the `PULSE_CHECK_{REPORT,COMPONENT,QUEUE}_BUDGET_SECONDS` overrides still win. The resolved values are reported under `inputs.collection_budget_seconds` so future timeouts are diagnosable from the report alone. title: t19154: perf(gh-transport): revalidate explicit-pagination pages with ETags so unchanged comment lists cost no REST quota
body:
## Summary

Explicit REST pagination (gh-rest-pagination-lib.sh) adds --include to read Link, which made every page ineligible for the GH#38566 conditional cache. In a 38-minute ledger sample it accounted for 1,402 of 3,517 quota-costing REST attempts (40%) with 0 revalidations, while ordinary governed GETs returned 304 49% of the time. Loop-owned page frames (marked AIDEVOPS_GH_PAGINATION_INCLUDE_OWNED=1) now store their whole frame. A frame replays on 304 only if it links onward (rel=next) or is a final raw JSON array shorter than min(per_page or 30, 100). Full final pages, --jq/--template final pages, field-encoded queries and notifications are never replayed, because a 304 carries no Link to reveal a newly appended page. Caller-requested --include stays ineligible.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh-rest-pagination-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/gh_conditional_cache.py, .agents/scripts/gh_conditional_request.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19154-brief.md

## Decisions

The final-page rule assumes GitHub's documented REST default of 30 and ceiling of 100. Endpoints whose ceiling is smaller (notifications: 50) are excluded, and --field queries fall back to the onward-link rule. jq-filtered final pages stay uncacheable; that can be a follow-up if the ledger shows material volume.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Live against GitHub using the worktree shim, run twice each: a single-page comments read (5 items, per_page=100) gave 200 then 304 with identical output. A three-page read (per_page=2) gave 200x3 then 304x3, and both runs returned [3,[2,2,1]]. After the gate refactor, a two-page read (per_page=3) gave 200x2 then 304x2 with identical [2,[3,2]], and caller-requested --paginate --include stayed live at 200x2 (gh-api-calls.log, caller=gh, route=explicit-rest-pagination). python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py: 16/16 OK, including a full-final-page no-replay case. test-gh-shim.sh: 335 passed. test-gh-api-instrument.sh and test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh passed. shellcheck is clean, and _ghrp_run is 100 lines.

Resolves #39233

title: t19157: feat(session-bus): issue watches relay worker/runner progress to interactive sessions; cross-runner who hint; worker pointers
body:
## Summary

Closes three session-bus blind spots found in the parallel-session audit. (1) Issue watches: an interactive root session can `watch-issue owner/repo#N` (tool action or CLI) for 7 days; the 2-minute worker-bus relay now runs a second pass (`worker-bus-relay-watches.sh`) that diffs status labels, assignees, closed/merged/reopened and new non-bot, non-ops comments, and sends each watching session one batched `info` pointer (never wakes, never writes GitHub, no titles or bodies). `claim-task-id.sh` watches the GitHub issues it creates when run from an OpenCode session (5 s, silent). `--new` watches report a worker pickup or closure that beat the first pass. Not-found items are reported once then skipped. (2) `who #N`/`PR#N` with no local match now names the `gh issue|pr view` read, since workers on other runners are not on this bus. (3) Headless Dispatch Rule 9: workers flag dependencies/overlaps in a comment on their own issue (watchers get it) and `aidevops sessions send` a one-line pointer when `who` shows a live local session. Also fixes the worker relay send-failure path: it advanced `checked`, so the next short listing could hide the unsent change, contrary to the documented 'failed send keeps the detection state'.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-watch.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-issue-watch.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-targets.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-watches.sh, .agents/workflows/full-loop.md, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19157-brief.md

## Decisions

Relay pass reuses the worker relay's lock, budget gate, listing (`since=`) and `_relay_issue_from_listing`, so cost is one listing per repo with due watches plus reads only on first sight or comment-count rise. Fresh baselines: creation labels vary (status:available default, explicit status:*, publication holds), so only status:queued/status:in-progress, closure and assignees present at the first check count as new. Watches live under the watching session (cap 50) and end with expiry, --off or presence loss; relay state is pruned to match. The GH#39130 linux-procfs --sudo-session check targets the D-Bus user session bus for approval kicks, not this aidevops message bus, so it does not apply. crossRunnerHint lives in session-bus-targets.mjs (added to the brief Files Scope).

title: GH#39251: chore: recover dirty worker worktree checkpoint
body:
## Summary

Fixes the flaky completion-mode drain test (GH#33747 test) reported as `failed` under host load.

**Root cause (product):** after the command exited 0, post-exit cleanup (`post_exit_cleanup`) used the same terminator as budget/cancel. It sent SIGTERM to the supervisor's own group and, after `killGraceMs`, SIGKILLed it (or `process.exit(1)`). Under load the drain outlasted `killGraceMs` (50 ms in the test), so the supervisor exited by signal/non-zero instead of the command's 0, and the manager recorded `failed`.

**Fix:**
- `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`: post-exit cleanup never signals the supervisor's own group and never self-SIGKILLs; the drain loop kills survivors individually. A later budget/cancel/signal request can still take over with full escalation. The GH#34047 `post_exit_descendants_terminated` flag is unchanged (set only for completion-triggered cleanup).
- `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`: under 2x CPU oversubscription, a second failure appeared (listener never wrote its pid within 3 s). Wait ceilings are now scaled (listener wait 9 s, budgets 15 s / 4 s expiry, terminal wait 10 s). They return early on success, so the unloaded runtime is unchanged.

## Verification

- Single test, 20 consecutive runs with `2 x CPU count` busy-loop processes: 0 failures (before the test-wait change: 1 of 20, `escaped server never listened`).
- `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`: exit 0 (twice).
- Not verified: macOS (run was on Linux). `bun run typecheck` is deferred to CI (tsc not installed on this runner).

Resolves #39251

title: t19160: fix(pulse): partial-continuation revisit walks past merged PRs that target a different issue
body:
## Summary

The periodic partial-continuation revisit walked an in-review issue's merged cross-referenced PRs newest first, but stopped at the first non-closing PR. Cross-references only prove a mention, so a newer merged PR with `For #<other>`, a prose mention, or an origin:interactive PR about other work ended the walk, and the older worker partial that targets the issue was never revisited. Adds `_pmpc_pr_may_own_issue`, which mirrors the guard's target resolution (closing, explicit For/Ref, title corroboration) from one body read. PRs that provably target another issue or none are skipped; PRs that may own the issue or have unreadable or ambiguous metadata still go to the unchanged guard. The walk is capped by `PULSE_PARTIAL_REVISIT_MAX_PRS` (default 10).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19160-brief.md

## Decisions

The guard `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` is unchanged and stays the single decision point. Uncertain metadata (unreadable body or title, ambiguous explicit refs, closing refs in unparsed forms) hands the PR to the guard, which ends the walk, matching the existing fail-closed stance (GH#38885).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` passes (240 PASS, 0 FAIL), including 9 new GH#39254 cases. Against the pre-change module, the skip and restore cases fail (verified with a temporary copy). `shellcheck` is clean. Runtime evidence: a bounded real-write drain on a managed product repository used the deployed guard with a walk-past loop. It processed 40 stranded `status:in-review` issues and restored 37 with `kind=merged-partial-continuation` markers; 11 of those needed walking past 2 to 6 newer merged PRs, which the old Pulse walk could not reach. Workers then re-dispatched the restored issues.

Resolves #39254

title: GH#39281: fix(pulse-merge): guarantee cursor progress and run a bounded CI-repair lane first
body:
## Summary

Root cause: on resume, the GH#38248 priority lane ran promoted merge-ready PRs before the cursor's resume item, so slow lane items could use up the graceful slice and the cursor never advanced (starvation). Failing-CI PRs also always sorted after merge-ready work, so CI repair for them was dispatched late. Changes: (1) the resume order is now [prefix minus lanes] + [resume item] + CI-repair lane + merge lane + tail, so the resume item is evaluated first and the cursor advances on every resume; (2) a bounded CI-repair lane (PULSE_MERGE_CI_REPAIR_LANE_LIMIT, default 2, 0 disables) promotes failing-CI PRs ahead of merge-ready work. A PR is promoted only when no current or legacy CI-repair lease exists for its head, it has not been evaluated in the lane at that head during this walk (.lane-ci-served), it is not the cursor's next PR, and it has no cached negative verdict; (3) durable cursor writes during the lane never rewind past processed PRs, and an unprocessed lane item is promoted again by a later resume; (4) lane records are cleared at walk end and ignored before a fresh walk; a failed reorder is now logged instead of failing silently. This changes ordering only: every merge gate is unchanged. Documented in workflows/pulse.md Priority Order.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-backlog-priority.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume.sh, .agents/workflows/pulse.md

## Decisions

Ran the resume item before promoted lanes rather than capping lane size, because only that guarantees forward progress whatever the lane cost. Used lease-directory presence (current and legacy keys) for CI-lane dedup instead of re-reading lease contents: this affects ordering only, so a cheap existence check is enough. The lane limit defaults to 2 to keep CI-repair dispatch responsive without starving merge-ready work.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Exercised the production _merge_ready_prs_for_repo / _pmp_sort_prs_by_backlog_priority paths with stubbed gh: test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume.sh (63/63) covers resume-item-first ordering, a newly failing PR joining the CI lane on resume, no-rewind cursor writes, and clearing lane records; test-pulse-merge-pr-backlog-priority.sh (41/41) covers lane bounds, current and legacy lease exclusion, served-head and resume-PR exclusion, stale-record handling, and limit 0. affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base: 30/30 selected suites pass at the final head. title: GH#39321: feat: schedule once recheck/snooze policy and failure advisories
body:
Resolves #39321

## What

`aidevops schedule once` runs one fresh worker at a due time. Follow-up checks ("recheck tomorrow, then again until it lands") need more than that: when the criteria are not met yet, they should snooze and try again later within bounds, close themselves when the criteria are met, and tell the operator when they give up. Today a follow-up that is not ready can only fail or succeed once, and a failure is visible only through `aidevops schedule status`.

Seen this session: a 24-hour hosting-incident recheck and an upstream PR review check both needed "check, and if not ready, check again later".

## Change

- `deferred-job-helper.sh once`: `--recheck-every DURATION` (min 5m), `--max-checks N` (default 6, max 100), `--until ISO-UTC`. Stored as a `recheck` object on the job. Refused for manual `--issue` dispatch, which cannot report a snooze.
- New `aidevops schedule snooze JOB_ID [--after DURATION] --reason TEXT`: only a running recheck job may snooze; the reason is reduced to one printable line.
- `deferred-job-runner.sh`: appends a check contract (job ID, check n of N, deadline, snooze command) to a private per-run prompt copy and exports `AIDEVOPS_DEFERRED_JOB_ID`. At the end of the run: a clean run without a snooze closes the job (`success`); a snooze or a failed run queues the next check while checks and the deadline remain; otherwise the job ends `failure`/`recheck_exhausted`.
- Terminal failures (including exhaustion and lease expiry) write `~/.aidevops/advisories/deferred-job-<JOB_ID>.advisory`, which session-start already surfaces (`aidevops-update-check.sh`). The text names the job, outcome and last reason only.
- `schedule status` shows a CHECKS column and a sanitized `recheck` object in JSON.
- Docs: `.agents/reference/routines.md` "Follow-ups and later checks" is the advised procedure; pointers from `.agents/scripts/commands/routine.md` and `.agents/reference/session.md` close-out step 3.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-runner.sh`, `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-deferred-job-helper.sh` (3 cases added to the existing suite)
- `.agents/reference/routines.md`, `.agents/reference/session.md`, `.agents/workflows/routine.md` (reached via `scripts/commands/routine.md`)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-deferred-job-helper.sh` → 18/18 pass (snooze requeue then close, exhaustion advisory plus failure retry, option validation).
- `shellcheck -x` clean on all four scripts; pre-commit ratchets pass.
- `markdownlint-cli2` clean on the three docs.
