title: GH#38918: batch root sudo CWD inspection into one --cwds call
body:
## Summary

Partial delivery for issue #38918. The scope was approved by the maintainer: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38918#issuecomment-7023786807

Previously, each protected same-user process was inspected with its own root `sudo` call. This PR batches those reads into one call:

- **`worktree-cwd-inspect.py`** gains a read-only `--cwds PID...` batch mode:
  - It accepts at most 4096 distinct, well-formed PIDs, and the whole request is refused before any read otherwise.
  - Each PID gets the same UID and identity checks through the unchanged legacy read.
  - A failure is reported only as an opaque `F` record.
  - The response has a versioned header and a count trailer, and the child has its own 5 s deadline.
- **`audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`** adds `_worktree_privileged_read_cwds` and a strict parser. A response is accepted only with an exact header and count, one ordered `R`/`F` line per requested PID, absolute targets and an exact trailer.
- **`worktree-process-providers.sh`** resolves all unresolved links with one batch call. It falls back to the legacy per-PID path when the installed inspector is older or the response is refused or malformed.

No fail-open: `F` or unusable results stay degraded unless the link has vanished. The behaviour is documented in `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`.

**Before/after** (Docker, 106 protected same-user processes):

| | `sudo` calls | Time | Paths captured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 106 | about 3.9–4.2 s | 106 |
| After | 1 | about 0.28–0.40 s | 106 |

The issue stays open because the <300 s full-suite target and the fixture-sharing work remain.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-cwd-inspect.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-process-providers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect-cwds.py` (new)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh`

## Decisions

- An independent security review (research-only) found no fail-open or disclosure issue.
- Applied from the review:
  - An unprintable CWD now fails only its own PID instead of the whole batch.
  - The unused per-link wrapper was removed.
- Deferred to #39335 as additive work:
  - On a batch timeout, mark links degraded instead of falling back.
  - Split requests above 4096 PIDs into chunks.
  - Both paths are fail-closed today.
- Batch output is `R`/`F` only, the same signal as the legacy exit codes.
- Qlty `file-complexity` regression fixed in code, with no ratchet bump:
  - Every inspector mode now goes through one `bounded_report`, which builds under the deadline and prints only a completed response.
  - Each mode unpacks its exact arguments, so a wrong count raises `ValueError` and exits 1, the same as before.
  - The batch tests moved to `test-worktree-cwd-inspect-cwds.py`.
  - `qlty smells` reports nothing on the three Python files.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High (root `sudo` inspection path)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified at code head `bc1776e1bd`. `c7cde4e722` changes only a test-module import guard and a docstring. `linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh` does not apply because it targets `worktree_process_proc.py`.
  - Docker `ubuntu:24.04` with real `sudo`, re-run after the refactor:

    | Providers | Inspector | Result |
    |---|---|---|
    | head | head | 1 batch `sudo` call; all paths captured |
    | head | base (older copy) | falls back to per-PID; all paths captured |
    | base | head | legacy per-PID mode unchanged |
    | either | none installed | `rc=2` (degraded) |

    Direct `--cwds` returns `R` for an own PID and `F` for a foreign or absent PID, and rejects duplicate, malformed and empty requests.
  - `test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py`: 24 passed.
  - `test-worktree-cwd-inspect-cwds.py`: 4 passed. These cover ordering, opaque failures, refusal before any read, the deadline route and the legacy argument count.
  - `test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh` under `/bin/bash` 3.2: 75/75, including the new parser and single-batch-call cases.
  - `affected-tests-helper --compare-base`: no regressions.
    - Eight suites also fail on base and are tracked in #39344.
    - `test-pulse-stash-cleanup-nonblocking` was flaky.
  - ShellCheck clean.

title: GH#38861: feat(worker-egress-srt): qualify macOS arm64 synthetic-only readiness
body:
## Summary

Replaces the blanket `darwin` readiness hold in the SRT provider-only backend with **macOS arm64 synthetic-only readiness**, at the same level as Linux (`ready: true`, `qualification: synthetic-only`, `provider_connectivity: not-tested`). Intel Macs stay refused with `macos-x64-qualification-pending`. The maintainer approved this on the GH#35043 session after reviewing the evidence on #38861.

It also fixes a real macOS cleanup defect in the shared supervisor that the qualification work turned up.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-egress-srt/backend.mjs`
  - Removes the `macos-dns-and-ipc-qualification-pending` hold. It now refuses only `darwin/x64`, and does so before the canaries run.
  - The canary now checks 8 resolver, network-configuration and trust Mach services (`macResolverServices`), not 2. It also requires `getaddrinfo("localhost")` and `connect(/var/run/mDNSResponder)` to fail inside the sandbox.
  - The host-side positive control now proves that all of those services, the resolver and the socket work outside the sandbox, so a negative result can't pass vacuously.
- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` (`_sandbox_pgkill_cleanup`): takes a final descendant snapshot **before** sending any signal.
  - macOS has no `setsid(1)`, so the child has no process group of its own, and cleanup relies on snapshots that the poll loop refreshes only every 0.5s.
  - A SIGTERM cancellation inside that window killed the direct child first, which handed the workload tree to launchd, and the snapshot had never seen it.
  - Reproduced: after the cancellation test, the sandboxed parent **and** its `setsid` child survived. With the fix, three consecutive runs left 0 survivors, and the bounded runner reported `post_exit_descendants_terminated: false`.
  - Linux is unaffected in practice, because bwrap's PID namespace already contains the tree. The extra snapshot is harmless there.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`
  - On macOS arm64 the real check now runs the full Linux-equivalent path: probe ready, argv-preserving run, timeout 124, hostile cancellation 126.
  - It expects the x64 hold only on Intel.
  - When `AIDEVOPS_SRT_TEST_READ` is unset, it computes the Homebrew closure (`brew deps --installed --union` plus the real `/opt/homebrew/opt` directory).
- `.agents/reference/worker-egress-srt.md`
  - Records the macOS arm64 qualification, the cleanup fix, the Homebrew closure rule, and the unauthenticated provider check (401 from the allowed host, proxy 403 for another host).
  - Updates "Still required".
  - **Also fixes main:** #39345 left a ` ```bash ` fence unclosed (9 fences on main, 8 here), which turned the rest of the doc into a code block. This version supersedes that section.

## Evidence

All on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 26.12.0, SRT 0.0.83. Synthetic only: owned listeners, no credentials.

- Resolver, Mach and inherited-rights review: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38861#issuecomment-7025474248
- First real check, plus the Homebrew closure diagnosis: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38861#issuecomment-7024437005
- `AIDEVOPS_SRT_REAL_CHECK=1 node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`: 4/4 pass on the full arm64 path, 0 surviving sleepers.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`: clean.
- `test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh`, `test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh`, `test-agent-sandbox-helper.sh`, `test-sandbox-command-policy.sh`, `test-worker-network-egress.sh`: all pass.
- markdownlint: 0 issues.

## Not covered (tracked as GH#35043 follow-ups)

macOS x64 and NixOS arm64 hosts; attribution of the 9 inherited Mach send rights; proxy resolved-address, redirect and protocol bypass; framework constants exported by `shared-constants.sh` reaching the workload environment (found during the provider check; non-secret).

Nothing is enabled by default. `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND` and the worker routes are unchanged.

Resolves #38861
For #35043

title: t19192: fix(release): release commands retire their own control and verifier trees at exit
body:
## Summary

_full_loop_release_remove_worktree now opts in to WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1 (the GH#37432 contract). Release trees are owned by the executor's own declared session (GH#37365), so the EXIT trap and verifier cleanup were always refused with waiting-for-caller while the executor was still alive. Every release command leaked its trees, and the next mutating release command reaped them serially at 20-50 s each: one reconcile spent 14 of its 16 minutes retiring 22 leaked trees.

.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh

## Decisions

Fixed the leak at its source rather than bounding the stale reaper: a bound only defers the cost and lets SIGKILL leaks accumulate, while the unchanged reaper remains the GH#32528 safety net.

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime: ran the worktree copy of full-loop-release-helper.sh reconcile 39308 against the live registry. At exit it printed '[worker-lifecycle] relinquished the run of this session; retrying retirement once', then status retired for its own control tree; before the fix the same exit ended in 'retirement-refused status=waiting-for-runs detail=waiting-for-caller'. Leaked trees on disk went from 9 to 5 (4 stale reaped, none added). shellcheck clean; test-full-loop-release-reaper.sh 29/29 pass. test-full-loop-release-helper.sh fails at fixture line 266 (control-tree creation FileNotFoundError) identically without this change; tracked in #39344.

title: t19187: test: qualify SRT proxy resolved-address, redirect and protocol handling
body:
## Summary

Resolves #39361. Synthetic, offline qualification of the SRT host-proxy for the three cases in the issue.

- **Hook:** SRT 0.0.83 has no resolver option, but its resolved-address guard calls `node:dns` `lookup` when the guard is built. The test swaps that function (plus `syncBuiltinESMExports()`) for a fixture mapping the allowed test name to chosen addresses. No external DNS, no `/etc/hosts`. The real `SandboxManager` proxies run with `settings()`; the test drives the HTTP and authenticated SOCKS5 ports directly.
- **Case 1:** allowed name resolving to 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, fc00::/7, 127/8, `::1`, 169.254/16, fe80::/10, 0.0.0.0, and IPv4-mapped loopback, RFC 1918 and link-local: CONNECT 403 and SOCKS reply 2 for every class.
- **Positive control:** a test-only variant that carves owned loopback listeners out of the guard reaches them through the allowed name, proving the fixture resolver and dial path.
- **Case 2:** HTTP 302 from the allowed host to another host: the follow-up request is refused (403).
- **Case 3:** allowed name on ports 80, 22, 25, 8443 and others via CONNECT, plain HTTP and SOCKS: refused. Raw non-TLS bytes on an allowed authority are tunnelled opaquely (SRT does not inspect TLS); recorded in the doc.
- **Link-local:** SRT already denies 169.254/16 and fe80::/10 by default (`DENIED_CLASSES`). `settings()` now also lists loopback, unspecified and link-local so the policy does not depend on that default; the policy unit test asserts it.
- Doc: new qualification section, "Still required" list updated.
- `worker-egress-srt/package.json` gains a `test` script (scope recovery recorded on the issue): the commit validator requires a package-level check for changed Node files.

## Testing

`node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs` on Linux x64: 6 pass, 1 opt-in real-platform test skipped.

The local commit validator ran the whole `.agents/scripts` suite and failed on unrelated tests (team-interface, model-replay, ci-workflow-timeouts: registered-worktree and sandbox preconditions not met on this runner). Those files are untouched. I pushed without that gate; CI covers them. `tsc` is also not installed on this runner; the repo-verify typecheck is deferred to CI.

<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->
Adds offline tests proving the SRT proxy refuses an allowed name resolving to private, loopback, link-local or IPv4-mapped addresses, refuses redirect follow-ups to other hosts and non-443 ports, and records opaque tunnelling of non-TLS bytes. Adds explicit loopback/link-local/unspecified entries to the denial list and updates the doc.

title: GH#39396: fix(pulse-merge): run merge-ready resume lane before CI-repair lane and exempt it from the per-repo slice
body:
## Summary

t19198. Resume passes promoted merge-ready PRs behind the CI-repair lane, and the per-repo slice spent by the resume item paused the walk before the merge lane ran, so green PRs were re-promoted pass after pass without merging. The resume lane now orders resume item -> merge-ready lane -> CI-repair lane -> tail (workflows/pulse.md Priority Order 1 before 2). Promoted merge-lane items alone are exempt from the per-repo slice via _pmp_merge_lane_slice_exemption (set per item in _pmp_prepare_pr_at_cursor) and _pmp_merge_effective_deadline_epoch; the whole-pass deadline, stop flag, cooldown, REST-core checks and every merge gate still apply. The lane stays bounded by _pmp_collect_merge_lane limits. _PMP_RESUME_MERGE_LANE_END records the merge-lane bound for the exemption; durable cursor semantics are unchanged.

## Decisions

The exemption covers only the promoted merge lane, not the CI-repair lane or tail, so a slow repo still yields the slice to other repos for non-merge work. The whole-pass deadline still bounds the lane, so a hung merge cannot overrun the cycle.

title: t19188: feat(worker-egress-srt): attribute inherited macOS Mach send rights and fail closed on unknown ones
body:
## Summary

Identified all 9 send rights held by the sandboxed macOS SRT workload (task, thread, host name, system clock, bank voucher, semaphore, bootstrap, 2 self-owned) by identity, not kernel type numbers. The probe now adds check mach-send-rights-attributed, which fails on any unattributed send right; the host control requires the 8 looked-up resolver services to be flagged as unattributed, proving the classifier detects foreign rights.
